items.title: What Car Salesmen Will Never Tell You
items.content_snippet: If you optimize your life long enough, you forget to live it. The cleanest evidence comes from Leaf Van Boven and Tom Gilovich, who asked people to recall a purchase over a hundred dollars, made either for an experience or for a material thing, and then asked which had made them happier. Experiences won. They won again when people were asked which purchase counted as money well spent. The reason sits in the adaptation. A jacket becomes furniture in your closet within a month. items.content_snippet: Memory-optimized Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) X2idn instances are now available in Asia Pacific (Hong Kong) Region. These instances, powered by 3rd generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors and built with AWS Nitro System, are designed for memory-intensive workloads and deliver improvements in performance compared to previous generation X1 instances. items.title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports model caching for faster inference autoscaling and reduced cold starts
items.content_snippet: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports model caching, an inference optimization that pre-loads model weights and container images onto cluster nodes so pods start in seconds instead of minutes. When running LLM inference at scale for workloads like chat assistants, agentic pipelines, RAG, and document analysis, cold start is a real bottleneck. items.title: AWS Lambda now supports direct read configuration for Amazon S3 Files
items.content_snippet: AWS Lambda now supports direct read configuration for Amazon S3 Files, letting you configure which storage your functions read from: S3 Files high-performance storage or your S3 bucket. With this launch, you can optimize the throughput and latency of file reads for your Lambda functions based on your application requirements. items.title: AWS HealthOmics now publishes real-time run metrics to Amazon CloudWatch
items.content_snippet: AWS HealthOmics now publishes real-time run metrics to Amazon CloudWatch, giving you visibility into workflow resource utilization as runs execute. The 14 new run metrics span CPU and GPU usage, memory usage, file system usage and I/O metrics, network throughput, and ephemeral storage usage. items.title: Building ambitious software — Jonathan Kelley, Dioxus Labs & Cognition
items.content_snippet: The Dioxus team got excited, maxed out their coding agent subscriptions, and turned out tens of thousands of lines of Rust covering features they had wanted for years. Almost none of it cleared the bar for merging. Those lines sat in draft, and Jonathan Kelley says they are sitting there still. He calls the failure mode becoming a slop cannon.
